author: KojaCola
body:
Hellooo Avicadians!



The Map Development team is happy to announce a build contest! The contest submissions will be open tomorrow, and will close on October 14th. We are really excited to see some awesome capture and destroy maps being made so we can spruce up our rotations! We also have a prize of 45% off any Avicus store purchase, as well as a 10$ Steam Gift-Card.  We will be showcasing the maps on October 22nd, which is when we will be having maps tested and scored, to determine a winner. After the maps are tested, the best maps will be put in a public rotation. We will also be hosting a temporary build server for the contest. Good luck and happy building! Here is some information for the contest:



General Info


Announced and information released: Sept. 16th

Submissions open: Sept. 17th

Submissions close: November 13th

Maps tested: TBA

Winner announced: TBA

Build Server IP: Below.


Prizes:


1st Place: $30 on Steam or Paypal AND 5 Setnext Gadgets

2nd Place: 5 Setnext Gadgets AND 45% off an Avicus purchase


Submission Rules:


  • Map must be by no more than three people.

  • Must be suitable for either the Capture or Destroy server.

  • Public maps only, team sizes must be 10v10 or larger.

  • Maps must be made for the contest, no maps from before or after.

  • Maps must include XML, or will be disqualified.

  • Maximum of 2 submissions per person.

  • Map developers may NOT help build maps. (Map developers are allowed to help with XML.)

  • Do not beg or annoy map developers or builders about doing XML for you; if you do so, your chances of winning will greatly decrease.

  • All submissions cannot be requested for removal from the Avicus map repository.

  • If you do not know how to XML, you can request Prodigy and Micah; they will help on a first come first serve basis.


Submission Format:


  • Map Name:

  • XML (Preferably posted to Pastebin or Hastebin):

  • Pictures (At least 5 in total; at least one must show a bird’s-eye view.):

  • Download (Preferably posted to Mediafire or Dropbox):

  • Authors:


Criteria for Judgement:


  • Gameplay

    • Match Duration (Max 20 points)

      • 0-5 Minutes: 5 points

      • 6-9 Minutes: 13 points

      • 10-13 Minutes: 18 points

      • 14-23 Minutes: 20 points

      • 24-30 Minutes: 19 points

      • 30-40 Minutes: 17 points

      • 40-∞ Minutes: 16 points


    • Average Judges’ Rating of Gameplay (Max 45 points)

      • Between 0 and 2: 5 points

      • Between 2 and 3: 10 points

      • Between 3 and 4: 15 points

      • Between 4 and 5: 20 points

      • Between 5 and 6: 25 points

      • Between 6 and 7: 35 points

      • Between 8 and 9: 40 points

      • Between 9 and 10: 45 points


  • Aesthetics

    • Average Judges’ Rating of Aesthetics (Max 20 points)

      • Between 0 and 2: 2 points

      • Between 2 and 3: 6 points

      • Between 4 and 5: 11 points

      • Between 5 and 6: 13 points

      • Between 6 and 7: 15 points

      • Between 7 and 10: 20 points


  • Originality

    • Average Judges’ Rating of Originality (Max 15 points)

      • Between 0 and 2: 2 points

      • Between 2 and 3: 6 points

      • Between 4 and 5: 8 points

      • Between 5 and 6.5: 10 points

      • Between 6.5 and 10: 15 points


  • Community Opinion

    • Average Rating (Max 20 points)

      • Between 0 and 1.36: 5 points

      • Between 1.37 and 2.28: 7 points

      • Between 2.29 and 2.80: 9 points

      • Between 2.81 and 3.29: 11 points

      • Between 3.30 and 3.49: 13 points

      • Between 3.50 and 3.64: 16 points

      • Between 3.65 and 3.73: 17 points

      • Between 3.74 and 3.94: 18 points

      • Between 3.95 and 4.49: 19 points

      • Between 4.50 and 5.0: 20 points


/120 Points Total


Good luck and have fun!

replies.body:
{tag=bf3319534f9243ee8abc7544b8234936} our contests were still better

and we never gave our scoring system to the public cause we wanted it to be simple. All we did was state what we wanted in maps and have no scoring cause it gets tough to read like this thread 

couple of things to mention cause I've held a couple of map contests when the server had 50+ hourly 

1) you should never rate a map based on map duration. This is solely based on the fact that maps have different duration times. One prime example is dust devils. Some matches can be 5 minutes. Others can be 3 hours. You should not be scoring based on duration csuse it depends on a) player count and b) who's online (I'm looking at those dust devil defenders in the back!)

2) the font that was used for the thread is ugly on avicus forums

3) why was enoki used for the banned instead of a more known map or a map that one a recent map contest (Apollo 13) to showcase previous map contests made (im not saying this is an issue but I'm legit curious lol)

4) why is there a maximum submission of ONE? I thought avicus needed maps and wouldn't you want an incentive to build? Sooooooooooo why limit to one?

5) community opinion shouldn't be based on only  rating but instead both the rating system and opinions in chat. Reasonings behind this is that not everyone uses the rating system and it'd be better off asking players something like "how was the map"

6) you'd need at least a 12v12 to a 20v20 to properly test maps for gameplay so you better get organizing! You'd need proper advertising. I hope you do so

7) give an example on "originality" so players can actually understand what you're talking about (to clarify users)

8) and your submissions rules are lacking. Map releases have a mandatory map.png and map_banner.png and make sure to notify map makers those resolutions and to use highest graphic settings when taking those pictures.

9) if you're hosting a build server, please have it open WHEN the contest goes live to make it easier for map makers to start building on that server instead of using an unreliable server or singleplayer to make it easier for users to start building.

10) boring title for a contest shaped for map making! Spice it up next time

11) why is there sorta a rule about begging map devs to create xml and a penalization system? Like if I'm a player waiting for my xml and it's been like 3 days and I was told the mapdevs can make my xml, I'd get impatient cause you guys told me you can make my xml yet you're not doing it! Just a thought I guess? 

12) is there a rule for contributors? Like I know I can have 3 authors  but can I have 3 authors and 6 contributors 

13) why do submissions close on a Saturday. You just threw away a perfect day for when players aren't at school to finish building maps (October 15th). If a contest starts on a Sunday, it should end on a Sunday.

14) who are the map judges? All the map devs? 2 mapdevs? 1 mapdev? Please clarify so everyone knows who they're up against during the gameplay rating system!!!!

15) prizes aren't the best. You can't get much with a $10 steam gift card and most regular players have donator ranks so there is no point to actually buy a rank cause there's no other worthy thing in the shop to get 


these are questions/enhancements that I suggest to future contests


good luck to those making maps

1) The penalties for having a map last too long are very minor. However, maps getting rushed is a real issue so by awarding less points to rushed maps, we would like to encourage mapmakers to think about gameplay and balance their maps.

replies.author: ViceTechnicolour
replies.body:
>All submissions cannot be requested for removal from the Avicus map repository.

This is why a lot of OCN map makers and Stratus map makers were turned off by your contests. You can feel free to argue as to why it's a good idea that you get rights to the map rather than the author, but as far as I'm concerned people have sent DMCAs to servers that take maps they don't have permission to any longer. You can't circumvent that, because if an author truly wants their map removed they have the ability to raise hell irregardless, whether they built the map or they coded it. From my understanding, it's happened to Minehut and a PGM clone server. 

Just let authors decide, making this a rule seems more intimidating.

EDIT: Why not just follow the conventions of the previous contests? They were (mostly) successful.

replies.author: _DISTRACTION_
replies.body:
The build server has been released! 

Build Server: 144.217.5.144:42000

Build Server Guide:

Once logged onto the server…

To create a world, use /create <world>
To open/enter the world, use /open <world>
To close a world, use /close <world>
To lock a world to its current ingame time, use /lock <world>
To delete a world, use /archive <world>
To get the download for a world, use /upload <world>

To help you build, the server has WorldEdit.

The build server is set up to save backups and allow for rollbacks. If any user is found to be griefing (or committing other malicious activities on the server), they will be banned from the build server, and barred from winning the contest.

IMPORTANT: You are not able to build within the 32x32 area around 0,0. In order to modify blocks in this area, you need to use WorldEdit. Use //pos1 and //pos2 to select an area, and then //set to set blocks.
